title: Axor Lab Regression
description: An EXECUTABLE INVARIANT derived from a trial (Suite Platform RFC §9). Not a governance concept: 'latency < threshold', 'budget <= limit', 'task_success == true', 'forbidden_tool_calls == 0', a gate verdict sequence and a custom evaluator outcome are all the same kind of object. A regression never carries natural language as its rule — `expectation` is prose FOR HUMANS and is never evaluated; `rule` is the machine-checked part. Superseded the governance-only pin: a pinned verdict sequence is now one rule kind among several.

status.description: paused = kept but not run; retired = intentionally no longer an invariant. A regression is never DELETED on failure — a failing invariant is a finding, not a bug in the invariant.

source.description: the trial this invariant was extracted FROM. Present for a pinned regression, absent for one that ships with a suite.

trace_ref.description: content hash of the frozen trace the pin was taken from

scenario_id.description: the pin replays under ITS OWN scenario's inputs — a multi-scenario bundle must not evaluate a pin against the wrong scenario

evidence_case_id.description: set when the regression was pinned from an EvidenceCase (the RFC's evidence → regression path)

rule.description: the machine-checked invariant. Exactly one kind.

expectation.description: prose shown in the Regression screen's Expectation panel. Documentation ONLY — never parsed, never evaluated. If it disagrees with `rule`, `rule` is what runs.

scope.description: which trials the invariant applies to. Absent = every trial in the run.

quantifier.description: all = every in-scope trial must satisfy the rule (the safe default); any = at least one must

history.description: append-only outcome log — the Regression screen's History panel

status.description: error = the invariant could not be EVALUATED (a malformed trace, a missing metric, an unresolvable kernel). Never collapsed into 'failed': not knowing is not the same as knowing it broke.

observed.description: the value actually seen, for a threshold rule

predicate_rule.description: a typed predicate/v1 evaluated over the trial's trace. This is the general case — the predicate language already expresses 'forbidden_tool_calls == 0' and 'task succeeded'.

expect.description: the required truth value of the predicate

metric_threshold_rule.description: a bound on a metric — 'latency < threshold', 'budget <= limit'. Reads trial.metrics (bundle/v1) or a suite-declared metric. An ABSENT metric yields history.status = 'error', never a silent pass: an unmeasured latency is not a fast one.

metric.description: a trial.metrics key or a suite metric name

aggregate.description: 'value' checks each in-scope trial individually (with scope.quantifier); anything else checks ONE number computed across the in-scope trials

verdict_sequence_rule.description: GOVERNANCE CAPABILITY. The pinned (trace, expected verdict sequence) that used to be the only regression kind. The WHOLE ordered sequence is pinned, not just the presence of a DENY, so a changed verdict order is still a change.

verdicts.description: the ordered gate verdicts the frozen trace must reproduce

kernel.description: the kernel the pin was taken under. Replaying under a different kernel is a counterfactual, and the result is reported as such rather than as a regression.

evaluator_rule.description: the outcome of a suite-declared evaluator (suite/v1 evaluation.evaluators)

expect.description: the required result; any JSON value, compared by canonical equality
